title: ACCESS IS4S curriculum research source ledger
scope: Current official federal sources and BC Indigenous adult-learning context for original learner and practitioner materials.
method: Direct official-page retrieval plus site searches and attempted general search. This is a curated evidence snapshot, not an exhaustive systematic review.
portability: All supplied-file paths are relative to this research directory. No full scraped text, private workspace paths or third-party research PDFs are included.

verification_status_meanings.content_retrieved_and_read: The stated content or sections were retrieved and examined; this is not a claim that every link or entire linked course was reviewed.
verification_status_meanings.retrieved_selective_inspection_only: File retrieved and selectively inspected; only the limited claims stated here are supported.
verification_status_meanings.not_verified_blocked: Content not accessed; no substantive claim supported.
verification_status_meanings.directory_listing_verified_report_not_re: Listing and description read, underlying report not read.

sources.title: Indigenous Skills for Success Journey, Planting the Seeds for Growth
claims: A train-the-trainer resource introduces Canada’s Skills for Success model from an Indigenous perspective for community, education, career and workplace practitioners.
The live landing page links a facilitator guide, participant workbook, course materials, and nine skill-specific learning tools.
Credit toward the Douglas practitioner program is conditional on taking the course with a certified instructor.
sources.claim_locator: What is the course about?; Who is the course for?; Free Downloads Of
limits: No claim our ACCESS materials are this course, qualify for its credit, or are endorsed by Douglas.
Linked videos, interactive course and approved facilitator list were not independently reviewed.
sources.rights_observation: No open licence verified; cite and link, do not assume reproduction permission.

sources.title: Indigenous Skills for Success Journey: Planting the Seeds for Growth — Facilitation Guide
claims: Printed pp4–5 acknowledge project partners and Indigenous advisory contributions; p4 names Carlene Quock of ACCESS on the advisory committee.
Printed p6 dedicates the course to John Webster, former CEO of ACCESS, and describes authentic Indigenous experiences as a basis for the course.
Printed pp7–10 identify practitioner audiences, individual journeys, reflection on participants’ contexts and values, and online/in-person/hybrid delivery.
Printed p9 describes the learning tools as definitions, video, reflection, practice activities and skills-coach review.
limits: Claims are about the Douglas course and its credited contributors, not approval of this ACCESS draft.
Reviewed front matter and selected delivery sections, not all 48 pages.
Do not reuse its Indigenous stories, artwork, framework imagery, worksheets or activity sequences as our own.
sources.rights_observation: Printed p1 / PDF p2: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, attribution required, noncommercial unadapted distribution only; adaptation requests go to Douglas. The guide also discusses adapting delivery, but this does not remove its explicit no-derivatives licence. Link for further study; do not bundle or adapt into this edition.

sources.title: Indigenous Student Services
claims: Supports self-identifying Indigenous students as self-directed independent learners; welcomes mature, new, returning, full-time and part-time students.
Lists individualized funding, community-referral, housing/childcare and academic supports; describes confidential voluntary self-identification.
Distinguishes Elders’ cultural/spiritual guidance from mental-health counselling.
sources.claim_locator: Indigenous Student Services; Services we provide; Self-identification
limits: Institutional services, eligibility and confidentiality statements apply to Douglas; do not promise them as ACCESS services.
Listed cultural activities are examples at Douglas, not directions for generic classroom ceremonies.
sources.rights_observation: No open licence verified; cite and link, do not assume reproduction permission.

sources.title: Indigenous Guides
claims: Identifies BCcampus’ Indigenization Professional Learning Series as a collaboration with the BC ministry.
States steering committee included Indigenous post-secondary leaders, FNESC, IAHLA and Métis Nation BC; guides authored by Indigenous and ally teams.
Links separate Pulling Together guides for foundations, teachers/instructors, frontline workers, leaders/administrators and curriculum developers.
limits: Verifies provenance and the existence of linked resources; contents and licences of the linked BCcampus books were not retrieved.
Does not establish FNESC, IAHLA or Métis Nation BC endorsement of our draft.
sources.rights_observation: No open licence verified; cite and link, do not assume reproduction permission.

sources.title: Protocol Welcome
claims: Distinguishes a host-Nation protocol welcome from a general acknowledgement; says the welcome can be offered only by a member of the First Nation whose territory hosts the event.
Explicitly states that not every Indigenous culture shares the same protocols or practices.
limits: BCIT institutional guidance is a source for respecting local authority; ACCESS must establish its own relationships and arrangements.
Do not transfer BCIT honorarium amounts, booking times or gift suggestions into universal requirements.
sources.rights_observation: No open licence verified; cite and link, do not assume reproduction permission.

sources.title: Land Acknowledgement
claims: Describes acknowledgement as recognizing historical and ongoing presence and relationships to land.
Distinguishes acknowledgement from protocol welcome and encourages personal learning and action.
limits: BCIT campus territory statements are location-specific; do not copy into ACCESS curriculum without confirming the location and local guidance.
sources.rights_observation: No open licence verified; cite and link, do not assume reproduction permission.

sources.title: Indigenous Modules
claims: Lists an Indigenous Awareness course with modules on Indigenous Peoples, Colonization and Decolonization, with external access through BCIT Free Online Learning.
limits: Course landing/registration and full course content were not retrieved; availability and any terms require checking before enrolment.
sources.rights_observation: No open licence verified; cite and link, do not assume reproduction permission.

sources.title: Indigenization
claims: Connects respect for cultures, languages and protocols with understanding historical, social and economic conditions.
Describes institutional responsibility across curriculum, policies, services and community partnerships.
limits: JIBC policy and public-safety context are not ACCESS policy.
sources.rights_observation: No open licence verified; cite and link, do not assume reproduction permission.

sources.title: Living Indigenization: Engagement Protocols & Guidelines
sources.publisher: Justice Institute of British Columbia; content credited to Heather Saranczak and Jason La Rochelle
claims: Printed pp12–15 emphasize dignity, agency, self-determination and context-specific engagement, including whether and how a community wishes to engage.
Printed p15 distinguishes First Nations, Inuit and Métis and explicitly considers migration and urbanization; there is no single way to be Indigenous.
Printed pp16–17 emphasize sustained relationships, reciprocity and respectful contribution.
limits: Institutional guidance, not a universal statement of every Nation’s protocols.
PDF has 13 pages with facing-page spreads; printed numbers differ from PDF positions.
Do not use demographic statistics from this source; no statistics were checked.
No Indigenous cultural review or community consent for this draft is implied.
sources.rights_observation: Printed p3 / PDF p2: ©2025 JIBC, all rights reserved; personal copying only, further reproduction/adaptation requires permission. Research copy remains in scratch evidence only; do not include PDF or artwork in deliverables.

sources.title: Skills for Success - Canada.ca
sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada, Government of Canada
sources.rights_observation: Official live webpage used through attributed summary and links; linked third-party materials retain their own terms. No scraped page content is distributed in this ledger.
sources.claim_locator: Main introduction, resources links, video transcript and page details
claims: Describes Skills for Success as foundational and transferable skills for employment.
The transcript names the nine skills, and the page links training, assessment, research and component/proficiency resources.
limits: This is the official introductory page, not an individual assessment or validation of the ACCESS materials.

sources.title: Skill components and proficiency levels - Canada.ca
sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada, Government of Canada
sources.rights_observation: Official live webpage used through attributed summary and links; linked third-party materials retain their own terms. No scraped page content is distributed in this ledger.
sources.claim_locator: Page introduction; skill-specific component and proficiency sections
claims: Provides skill definitions, components and proficiency descriptions for all nine Skills for Success.
Says organizations can adapt the resources for curricula, training and assessment, and that the Skills for Success Program will refine proficiency levels over time.
Links a separate Skills for Success Proficiency Levels Development research report.
limits: The linked SRDC report was not independently retrieved or read.
The page is a current online source snapshot; it does not validate the local classroom feedback statuses or turn the original activities into a standardized assessment.
Source component labels reproduced in the books are attributed to the supplied March 2024 SkillPlan guide; small wording differences from the current federal page should not be silently erased.

sources.title: Research Reports - Canada.ca
sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada, Government of Canada
sources.rights_observation: Official live webpage used through attributed summary and links; linked third-party materials retain their own terms. No scraped page content is distributed in this ledger.
claims: Lists Skills for Success Proficiency Levels Development (2024), attributed to SRDC, and says the study produced resources for further development of proficiency descriptors.
Lists a 2023 implementation-guidance item, a 2022 Indigenous foundational/transferable-skills item attributed to Northern Policy Analytics, and the 2021 SRDC launch report.
limits: These are verified directory listings and descriptions, not independently read research findings.
The 2024 report and descriptor tables were not retrieved; no claim about their full contents or a replacement validated proficiency scale is made.

The directory label and destination link for the 2023 implementation-guidance item should be checked before use; the retrieved destination path names a launch report. Do not silently treat the directory title as verified report metadata.
Do not merge the directory’s 2023 label with SkillPlan’s 2022 bibliography entry without checking the underlying publication.

sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada, Government of Canada
sources.rights_observation: Official live webpage used through attributed summary and links; linked third-party materials retain their own terms. No scraped page content is distributed in this ledger.
sources.claim_locator: Introduction and disclaimer; Indigenous Skills for Success Journey course and learning-tools entries
claims: Lists assessment and training tools from government and external organizations, with audience, skill, delivery and cost information.
Lists Douglas College’s Indigenous Skills for Success Journey course and learning tools, leading to the directly retrieved Douglas resources in this ledger.
Explicitly states the government does not endorse third-party websites or guarantee their content.
limits: Directory inclusion is not government endorsement of a tool or this ACCESS edition.
Costs, availability, licences, certification and suitability must be checked on the actual provider’s current resource.
The URL has a Training query parameter, but the extracted page includes the directory data; no claim is made that every entry was individually inspected.

design_sources.title: ACCESS Numeracy Hub — observed design implementation
claims: Observed hub CSS uses background #F7F4F1, ink #1A1512, red #D2181F and gold #FFBC00.
Observed font tokens name Archivo, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono.

Brand notes call the type pairing recommended rather than confirmed by ACCESS.
No new Nation-specific artwork, cultural pattern or third-party guide artwork is licensed through this source.
